title: Effects of integrating peer assessment with electromechanical game-based learning on enhancing AI learning and computational thinking of undergraduates
sourceFileName: 6. Effects of integrating peer assessment with electromechanical game-based learning on enhancing AI learning and computational thinking of undergraduates.pdf

segments.sourceText: ABSTRACT Peer assessment and AIoT board games have emerged as effective game-based learning approaches for enhancing artificial intelligence (AI) education and computational thinking (CT). This study employs a four-group quasi-experimental design to examine their impact on undergraduate learning using a personal audio classifier (PAC). The AIoT board game integrates CT and AI concepts through collaborative, hands-on learning, incorporating peer assessment, problem-solving scenarios, and paired programming. Results indicate that anonymous online peer assessment fosters critical thinking and reduces learning anxiety. The AIoT board game enhances collaboration, creativity, and the practical application of AI concepts. Peer assessment further supports iterative improvement of PAC applications for gameplay. The integration of peer assessment within problem-solving tasks significantly improves learning outcomes, lowering barriers to AI education and preparing students for a technologydriven future. This study highlights the potential of combining AI instructional tools with peer assessment to deepen students’ understanding of AI and CT.

The development of these technologies has significantly altered our societal perceptions and perspectives, necessitating the cultivation of individuals’ abilities to operate or comprehend these technologies. One of the most fundamental and pivotal concepts therein is computational thinking (CT). In contemporary society, CT has evolved into an indispensable foundational skill for individuals (Yadav et al., 2014).

segments.sourceText: Research suggests that utilizing game-based learning can enhance and sustain students’ motivation (Alt, 2023) and engagement (Clark et al., 2016). Properly designed educational game content can facilitate deeper student thinking. In recent years, numerous researchers have integrated the concept of board games into education. Gee (2005) indicated that by establishing clear learning objectives, board games can become effective tools for promoting self-directed learning, problem solving, and in-depth learning. Due to their collaborative nature, board games enable students to experience educational content through social interaction, peer engagement, and mutual learning (Wu et al., 2014). Board games, as an educational tool, are also regarded as an important medium for practicing computational thinking (Bayeck, 2023). On the other hand, research on AI education points out that visualizing and gamifying AI course materials can effectively enhance students’ learning interest (DeNero & Klein, 2010).

segments.sourceText: The primary value of peer assessment lies in the close interaction among peers. Chang et al. (2021) showed through meta-analysis that peer assessment can effectively improve students’ learning effectiveness. In typical classroom scenarios, the number of students often far exceeds that of teachers, resulting in limited individual feedback from instructors. Peer assessment serves as a solution to this predicament, as research indicates that peer feedback can be more direct and personalized compared to feedback from teachers (Topping, 2009). From another perspective, teacher feedback is often perceived by students as authoritative and less open to challenge, while peer feedback tends to be more diverse. Furthermore, peer feedback can foster interactive discussions among students, even to the extent of promoting mutual engagement (Cole, 1991; Zhan et al., 2022).

segments.sourceText: CT has been recognized as a fundamental twenty-first-century competency that supports logical reasoning, problem solving, and innovation across disciplines (Voogt et al., 2015). Wing (2006) first conceptualized CT as a cognitive process of applying computer-science principles to formulate problems and design solutions that can be executed by humans or machines. Wing (2011) further emphasized abstraction as the core cognitive mechanism that enables the transfer of computational reasoning to diverse real-world contexts.

segments.sourceText: Barr and Stephenson (2011) subsequently extended CT into a broader set of nine conceptual abilities: data collection, data analysis, data representation, decomposition, abstraction, algorithmic thinking, automation, parallelization, and simulation. These dimensions reflect the multidimensional nature of CT in the problemsolving process. Later, Selby and Woollard (2013) synthesized these conceptualizations into four essential elements: logical thinking processes, abstraction, decomposition, and problem-solving patterns. Their work clarified the interconnections among CT subskills and laid a foundation for pedagogical implementation.

segments.sourceText: Building on these developments, BBC proposed a more pedagogically practical and measurable framework that defines CT as the ability to give precise instructions to a computer on what to do next. The BBC model operationalizes CT through four key dimensions, namely decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithms, and provides a clear structure for classroom instruction and assessment. Compared with earlier frameworks that emphasized theoretical breadth, the BBC framework is concise, teachable, and directly applicable to computational learning activities. Because of its pedagogical clarity and applicability, this study adopted the BBC framework as the foundation for instructional design. All subsequent course activities and assessment instruments were developed based on this framework to ensure that each stage of learning incorporated the four CT dimensions, enabling students to decompose problems, recognize patterns, abstract core principles, and design algorithms to address authentic learning challenges.

translation.faithfulZh: 基於這些發展，BBC 提出了一個更具教學實用性和可衡量的框架，將 CT 定義為向計算機提供精確指示的能力，說明下一步該做什麼。 BBC 模型透過分解、模式識別、抽象和演算法四個關鍵維度實現 CT 操作，併為課堂教學和評估提供了清晰的結構。 與強調理論廣度的早期框架相比，BBC 框架簡潔、可教且直接適用於計算學習活動。 由於其教學清晰度和適用性，本研究採用 BBC 框架作為教學設計的基礎。 所有後續課程活動和評估工具都是基於該框架開發的，以確保學習的每個階段都結合了四個 CT 維度，使學生能夠分解問題、識別模式、抽象的核心原則和設計演算法，以應對真實的學習挑戰。

The use of board games for developing educational competencies is not a contemporary phenomenon; its origins can be traced back to as early as 2200 BC. Many schools in a certain city in the United States have incorporated games such as Monopoly and Checkers to enhance students’ mathematical skills. Oktaviane et al. The results found that competitive board games have a positive impact on students and make learning full of interactions and interesting.

segments.sourceText: Compared to traditional learning, incorporating educational board games into the curriculum can further aid students in developing logical thinking, critical thinking, and deductive reasoning skills (Hinebaugh, 2009). In the past, many subjects such as mathematics, language, history, and science have been taught using conventional methods. However, in order to enhance learning effectiveness, motivate students, and pique their interest, educators have infused elements of board games into the curriculum. This integration allows students to engage in communication with others through board games, thereby enhancing their interpersonal communication skills (Charlier & De Fraine, 2013). On another note, Cheng (2018) employed educational board games for language learning, revealing that such an approach effectively improved students’ learning effectiveness while also reducing their learning anxiety.

segments.sourceText: Peer assessment is a mode of evaluation whereby learners assess one another, typically those with similar levels of learning, and has been successfully applied in primary, middle, and high schools, even among very young students and those with special educational needs or learning disabilities (Ehly & Topping, 1998). Furthermore, a substantial body of research demonstrates that peer assessment enhances learning effectiveness (Cartney, 2010; Cartney & Rouse, 2006; Cassidy, 2006; Clegg & Bryan, 2006; Panadero et al., 2016; Topping et al., 2000). Importantly, both assessors and those being assessed benefit from this process. They can identify their own shortcomings through evaluating their peers’ work, and can also recognize others’ weaknesses, leading to improvement (Yorke, 2003; Zhan et al., 2023). However, in countries where the primary educational approach involves teacher guidance and does not encourage independent thinking, students may not be receptive to peer assessment (Topping, 2023).

translation.faithfulZh: 同伴評估是一種評估模式，學習者彼此評估，通常是具有相似學習水平的人，並已成功應用於小學、初中和高中，即使在非常年輕的學生和有特殊教育需求或學習障礙的學生中也是如此（Ehly & Topping，1998）。 此外，大量研究表明，同伴評估可以提高學習效果（Cartney, 2010; Cartney & Rouse, 2006; Cassidy, 2006; Clegg & Bryan, 2006; Panadero et al.，2016；Topping et al.，2000）。 重要的是，評估員和被評估的人都從這個過程中受益。 他們可以透過評估同行的工作來識別自己的缺點，也可以識別他人的弱點，從而導致改進（Yorke，2003；Zhan et al.，2023）。 然而，在小學教育方法涉及教師指導並且不鼓勵獨立思考的國家，學生可能無法接受同伴評估（Topping，2023）。

segments.sourceText: In online peer assessment, Cheng and Tsai (2012) found that higher psychological safety, lower goal value diversity, greater trust in oneself as an assessor, and more positive social interdependence contribute to cultivating deeper learning. An important feature of online peer assessment is its anonymity, which presents both advantages and disadvantages (Li, 2017). Previous research has indicated that anonymous peer assessment seems to offer advantages in terms of students’ perceptions of the learning value of peer assessment. segments.sourceText: Despite the positive findings, this study has several limitations. First, EG2 was conducted online due to the COVID-19 pandemic, whereas the other groups were conducted face-to-face. This difference in modality may have confounded the effects of peer assessment, particularly with respect to cooperative learning outcomes. Second, the learning achievement test showed relatively low reliability (KR-20 values below .70), which may have introduced measurement errors. Although the CT self-efficacy scale demonstrated acceptable internal consistency after item selection, further validation studies are recommended to strengthen its applicability in different contexts. Finally, the short intervention period of two weeks (six hours in total) is acknowledged as a limitation, since cultivating higher-order thinking skills such as critical and computational thinking requires repeated practice, iterative reflection, and longer-term engagement (Voogt et al., 2015; Wing, 2011). Shortterm interventions may primarily influence surface-level behaviors, such as modifying assignments according to criteria, rather than fundamentally reshaping thinking modes. Future studies should therefore adopt extended interventions, incorporate repeated practice cycles, and include delayed post-tests to capture the gradual and sustained development of higher-order thinking, in line with the progressive nature of educational learning processes.
